+import dataset
+import unittest
+
+class TestUpsertIdFix(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_upsert_with_id_does_not_create_duplicate_index(self):
+        """Test that upsert with 'id' as key doesn't try to create a duplicate index."""
+        db = dataset.connect('sqlite:///:memory:')
+        table = db['test_table']
+        
+        # This should not raise an exception
+        data = dict(id=1, name='test')
+        table.upsert(data, ['id'])
+        
+        # Verify data was inserted
+        result = table.find_one(id=1)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
+        self.assertEqual(result['name'], 'test')
+        
+        # Verify we can update
+        data2 = dict(id=1, name='updated')
+        table.upsert(data2, ['id'])
+        
+        result2 = table.find_one(id=1)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result2)
+        self.assertEqual(result2['name'], 'updated')
+        
+    def test_upsert_with_multiple_keys_including_id(self):
+        """Test upsert with multiple keys including 'id'."""
+        db = dataset.connect('sqlite:///:memory:')
+        table = db['test_table_multi']
+        
+        # This should not raise an exception
+        data = dict(id=1, category='A', value=100)
+        table.upsert(data, ['id', 'category'])
+        
+        # Verify data was inserted
+        result = table.find_one(id=1, category='A')
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
+        self.assertEqual(result['value'], 100)
+        
+        # Verify we can update
+        data2 = dict(id=1, category='A', value=200)
+        table.upsert(data2, ['id', 'category'])
+        
+        result2 = table.find_one(id=1, category='A')
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result2)
+        self.assertEqual(result2['value'], 200)
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()
